title: Price a detail job profitably (cost-plus, not guess)
problem: Most detailers eyeball pricing or copy competitors and undercut by 25%+, losing money once you account for labor, chemicals, equipment depreciation, fuel (mobile), insurance, and self-employment tax. Without a cost-plus formula they cannot tell whether a $250 full detail actually nets $80 or -$30.
who: Solo mobile detailers, new shop owners (first 3 years), part-time detailers transitioning to full-time

skill_spec.name: Detail Job Price Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Computes minimum profitable price for a detail job using cost-plus formula with vehicle type, services, location, and target margin

inputs.name: monthly_overhead
inputs.label: Monthly overhead USD (insurance, rent, software, depreciation)

outputs.name: recommended_price
outputs.label: Recommended price with target margin USD

outputs.name: breakdown
outputs.label: Labor / Materials / Overhead / Fuel / Tax allocation

outputs.name: se_tax_set_aside
outputs.label: Self-employment tax to set aside (15.3%) USD

skill_spec.formula_hint: price = (labor_hours * hourly_target_rate) + material_cost + (monthly_overhead / monthly_jobs_avg) + (miles * 0.67 IRS rate) + se_tax_buffer; then markup by target_margin_pct

example_queries: Price a 2-stage paint correction + 5yr ceramic on a black Audi Q5, 12 hours labor, $180 in chemicals, mobile job 18 miles round-trip
What should I charge for an interior detail on an SUV with pet hair, 3 hours work?
Am I making money at $200 for a full detail with 4 hours of labor and $35 in supplies?

title: Quarterly estimated tax + self-employment tax calculation
problem: Solo mobile detailers and shop owners are 1099 self-employed and owe 15.3% SE tax plus federal income tax on net profit. Most don't set aside cash quarterly, miss Form 1040-ES deadlines (Apr/Jun/Sep/Jan), and face penalty + interest plus a 5-figure April surprise bill.
who: Solo mobile detailers, 1099 shop owners, side-hustle detailers earning >$400/year net

skill_spec.name: Detailer Quarterly Tax Estimator
skill_spec.one_liner: Computes quarterly federal estimated tax, SE tax, and state income tax with deductible expenses for auto detailers

inputs.name: deductible_expenses_ytd
inputs.label: Deductible business expenses USD (chemicals, equipment, mileage, insurance, software)

outputs.name: se_tax_due
outputs.label: SE tax due (15.3% on 92.35% of net) USD

outputs.name: underpayment_penalty_risk
outputs.label: Safe harbor status (90% current / 100-110% prior year)

skill_spec.formula_hint: se_taxable = net_profit * 0.9235; se_tax = se_taxable * 0.153; quarterly = (annual_proj_tax * 0.25) - paid_prior_quarters

example_queries: I'm a mobile detailer in Texas, $48K gross YTD, $18K expenses, what's my Q3 estimated payment?

title: EPA stormwater compliance checklist (avoid wash-water Clean Water Act fines)
problem: Mobile detailers and shops dumping wash water into storm drains face Clean Water Act civil penalties up to $64,618/day per violation. Most owners don't know the BMP rules (water-containment mats, reclamation, sanitary sewer disposal), local stormwater ordinance specifics, or when NPDES permit is required. EPA has shut down mobile detailers.
who: All mobile detailers, shop owners with parking-lot bays, body shop detail divisions

skill_spec.name: Detailer Stormwater Compliance Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step Clean Water Act compliance for wash water capture, reuse, and disposal customized by state and operation type
steps: Step 1: Identify if operation is mobile, fixed shop, or hybrid - determines BMP requirements
Step 2: Check state stormwater authority (EPA direct or state-delegated NPDES) - varies by state
Step 3: Determine if NPDES permit (MSGP) required - generally yes for industrial facilities, no for residential mobile under exemption
Step 4: Install water containment - berms, mats (CycloneVac, Water Wall), or dedicated wash pad with sump
Step 5: Set up wash water reclamation OR sanitary-sewer discharge agreement with POTW (publicly owned treatment works)
Step 6: NEVER discharge to storm drains, curbs, gutters, creeks - violation regardless of soap type
Step 7: Document BMPs in written Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) if MSGP-permitted
Step 8: Train all employees on BMPs and document training annually
Step 9: Audit chemical inventory - phase out PFAS-containing products by 2025-2027 in CA/ME/MN/NY
Step 10: Keep SDS binder for all chemicals (also OSHA 1910.1200 requirement)
Step 11: For mobile: carry water reclamation system (vacuum + filtration) on rig OR work only on permeable surfaces (grass, gravel) with biodegradable soap (still risky)
Step 12: Photograph job site before/after - proof of no runoff if disputed
warnings: Biodegradable soap is NOT a defense - CWA prohibits ANY non-stormwater discharge to drains regardless of toxicity
Working on customer's driveway is YOUR liability if runoff reaches storm drain
CA, NY enforcement most aggressive; TX, FL less but penalties same federal
PFAS bans (CA AB 2771 cosmetics analog being extended) - check label for PFOS/PFOA

example_queries: Mobile detailer in California - how do I stay legal on driveway washes?
Do I need an NPDES permit for my 3-bay detail shop in Houston?
What's the actual fine if EPA catches me washing on a customer's driveway with no containment?

title: California Car Wash and Polishing Act registration + bond compliance
problem: California requires annual $300 registration + $15,000 surety wage bond for any car wash/detail business with employees under the Car Washing and Polishing Act. Solo mobile = exempt. Operators routinely miss renewal, skip the bond, or misunderstand exemption - resulting in $100/day penalties, back-wage liability, and Labor Commissioner investigations.
who: California shop owners, mobile detailers with 1+ employee or 1099 helper, dealership detail managers

skill_spec.name: California Car Wash Act Compliance
skill_spec.one_liner: Walks through annual registration, bond filing, wage compliance, and renewal requirements under Labor Code 2050-2067
steps: Step 1: Determine if Car Wash Act applies - business that washes/polishes vehicles for compensation with 1+ employee in California
Step 2: Confirm exemption status - solo mobile no-employee = exempt; charities, dealerships own lot, self-serve washes = exempt
Step 3: Obtain $15,000 surety bond minimum (higher if >$50K monthly wages) from authorized surety bond company
Step 4: File Form CWP-1 Application for Registration with DLSE - $300 annual fee
Step 5: Post Notice to Employees at workplace in English, Spanish, Mandarin, Vietnamese, Korean, Tagalog as applicable
Step 6: Maintain payroll records 4+ years - pay stubs, hours, deductions, piece rate if applicable
Step 7: Pay employees per California minimum wage ($16+/hr 2026, higher in some cities) - no piece-rate workarounds without compliant rest/recovery pay
Step 8: Provide written paystubs every pay period (Labor Code 226)
Step 9: Submit annual renewal by anniversary date - missing = $100/day penalty + closure risk
Step 10: Display registration certificate visibly in workplace
Step 11: If hiring 1099 'independent contractor' detailer - apply AB 5 ABC test; likely misclassification, treat as W-2
warnings: Bond covers unpaid wages - if employee files claim, surety pays then comes after you for reimbursement
Misclassifying detailers as 1099 contractors under AB 5 = ~$25,000+/worker penalties + back wages + benefits
Labor Commissioner has subpoena power and investigates wage complaints aggressively
Bond amount increases with payroll size - check threshold annually

example_queries: I just hired my first detailer in LA - what do I file with the state?
My CA car wash registration expired last month, what penalties am I looking at?
Am I exempt as a solo mobile detailer with one 1099 helper on weekends?

title: Chemical inventory + reorder + PFAS compliance tracker
problem: Detailers waste 10-20% on chemicals via over-ordering, expiration, and theft. They also need to track which products contain PFAS (banned in CA/ME/MN/NY starting 2025-2027) and maintain SDS binder for OSHA HazCom. Manual spreadsheet tracking fails. Result: surprise stock-outs, expired product, OSHA fines $16K+/violation.
who: Shop owners with $500+/mo chemical spend, ceramic/PPF installers, multi-tech operations

skill_spec.name: Chemical Inventory + Compliance Tracker
skill_spec.one_liner: Weekly inventory routine with PFAS flagging, SDS verification, expiration tracking, and reorder-point logic
steps: Step 1: Pull current SDS from manufacturer for every chemical SKU (annual refresh per OSHA 1910.1200)
Step 2: Tag each product with state-applicability flag - check Section 3 (Composition) for PFAS/PFOS/PFOA
Step 3: Photograph or scan each bottle - lot number, mfr date, expiration if printed
Step 4: Measure current volume (visual or weight) vs full container
Step 5: Compare to weekly usage rate - flag low-stock SKUs against reorder point (usage_rate * lead_time_days * safety_factor 1.5)
Step 6: Discard expired or visually degraded product - log disposal route (sanitary sewer permitted? hazardous waste pickup?)
Step 7: Update SDS binder with any new product additions before first use
Step 8: Verify GHS labels on all secondary containers (spray bottles) - product name + hazard pictograms required
Step 9: Quarterly: review for PFAS phase-out compliance in affected states
Step 10: Annual: confirm employee HazCom training documented (date + topics + employee signature)
warnings: OSHA inspection finds unlabeled secondary spray bottle = serious violation up to $16,131
PFAS in tire dressing / glass coating common - check labels carefully
Hydrofluoric acid wheel cleaners - high-hazard, special handling, often regulated locally
Mixing ammonia + bleach (some interior cleaners) = chloramine gas - never combine

title: Damage claim response (customer alleges scratches/damage)
problem: Customer calls 2 days after detail claiming scratches/dents/electronic issue caused by detailer. Owner panics, GL deductible $500-$1000, possible insurance claim history affecting renewal. Wrong response (refunding without investigation, admitting fault in text) makes it worse. Need step-by-step protocol.

skill_spec.name: Customer Damage Claim Response Protocol
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step response when a customer alleges post-service damage, protecting business while resolving fairly
steps: Step 1: STAY CALM - acknowledge claim, do NOT admit fault in writing or text yet
Step 2: Schedule in-person inspection within 24-48 hours - in daylight, outdoors
Step 3: Pull intake photos from job - compare against claimed damage location
Step 4: Photograph current condition thoroughly - all angles, close-up of claim area, wide context
Step 5: Verify alignment - does claimed damage match a tool/process actually used? (e.g., swirls vs PPF edge)
Step 6: If pre-existing (visible in intake photos) - politely show evidence to customer with copies of intake doc
Step 7: If genuinely caused by detail - acknowledge, propose remedy (repair quote from body shop, redo service, partial refund) - get written agreement before payment
Step 8: For claims >$1000 or insurance involvement - notify GL carrier within policy notice window (usually 30 days)
Step 9: Document everything in writing - timeline, photos, communications - email summary back to customer
Step 10: If customer threatens chargeback - contact payment processor with evidence package immediately
Step 11: Small claims threshold - varies by state ($5K-$25K) - know your state's process
Step 12: Update intake process - what gap let this through? More photos? Better waiver?
warnings: Never text 'I'm so sorry' or 'I'll cover whatever you need' - these are admissions
Refunding without investigation invites pattern abuse (customer tells friends)
Insurance claims affect renewal - low-dollar settle out of pocket if clearly your fault
Defamation note: customer leaving false review = potential legal claim but usually not worth pursuing

example_queries: Customer says I scratched her hood - texted me a photo. What do I do?
Pulled the intake form, swirl marks customer is now complaining about were there before. How do I handle this?
